meta.note: Seed set of verified PYQs. Add more questions from the official UPSC PDFs by following the same object shape. Each option index is 0-based; 'answer' is the index of the correct option.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: The mind of the makers of the Constitution of India is reflected in which of the following?
options: The Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.explanation: The Preamble is regarded as the key to the Constitution and reflects the ideals, objectives and philosophy the framers intended. It embodies the source of authority (the people), the nature of the state, its objectives and the date of adoption, making it the truest reflection of the makers' mind.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement?
options: Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment Act
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed in Part III
Article 24 and the provisions under the 44th Amendment Act
questions.explanation: In K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court held that the Right to Privacy is an intrinsic part of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21 and is also traceable to the various freedoms guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: In the context of India, which one of the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties?
options: Rights are personal and hence independent of society and duties
Rights are not personal and hence associated with society
Duties, not Rights, are important for the stability of the State
questions.explanation: Rights and duties are correlative: every right of one person implies a corresponding duty on others (and on the state) to respect it. A right without a corresponding duty is meaningless, which is why the two are treated as two sides of the same coin.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question:
Which of the following are the discretionary powers given to the Governor of a State?
1. Sending a report to the President of India for imposing the President's rule
2. Appointing the Ministers
3. Reserving certain bills passed by the State Legislature for consideration of the President of India
4. Making the rules to conduct the business of the State Government
questions.explanation: Reporting to the President for President's Rule (Art. 356) and reserving bills for the President's consideration (Art. 200) are discretionary powers. Appointing Ministers is done on the CM's advice, and rules of business are made on ministerial advice, so 2 and 4 are not discretionary.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question:
Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the 'Rule of Law'?
1. Limitation of powers
2. Equality before law
3. People's responsibility to the Government
4. Liberty and civil rights
questions.explanation: Rule of Law (Dicey) implies limitation/supremacy of law over arbitrary power, equality before law, and protection of liberty and civil rights. 'People's responsibility to the Government' inverts the relationship — under Rule of Law the Government is responsible to the people and the law.

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
With reference to the difference between the culture of Rigvedic Aryans and Indus Valley people, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Rigvedic Aryans used the coat of mail and helmet in warfare whereas the people of Indus Valley Civilization did not leave any evidence of using them.
2. Rigvedic Aryans knew gold, silver and copper whereas Indus Valley people knew only copper and iron.
3. Rigvedic Aryans had domesticated the horse whereas there is no evidence of Indus Valley people having been aware of this animal.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indus people knew gold, silver and copper but did NOT know iron — iron came into use only in the later Vedic period, so describing them as knowing 'copper and iron' is incorrect.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: With reference to the history of ancient India, Bhavabhuti, Hastimalla and Kshemeshvara were famous
questions.explanation: All three were noted Sanskrit playwrights/dramatists. Bhavabhuti (8th century) wrote Uttararamacharita and Malatimadhava; Hastimalla and Kshemeshvara were also dramatists of the classical Sanskrit tradition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which one of the following is the best description of the term 'ecosystem'?
options: A community of organisms interacting with one another
That part of the Earth which is inhabited by living organisms
A community of organisms together with the environment in which they live
The flora and fauna of a geographical area
questions.explanation: An ecosystem is a community of interacting organisms (the biotic component) together with the physical environment (the abiotic component) with which they interact. Option (b) describes the biosphere, not an ecosystem.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The 2004 Tsunami made people realize that mangroves can serve as a reliable safety hedge against coastal calamities. How do mangroves function as a safety hedge?
options: The mangrove swamps separate the human settlements from the sea by a wide zone in which people neither live nor venture out
The mangroves provide both food and medicines which people are in need of after any natural disaster
The mangrove trees are tall with dense canopies and serve as an excellent shelter during a cyclone or tsunami
The mangrove trees do not get uprooted by storms and tides because of their extensive roots
questions.explanation: Mangroves have extensive, dense root systems (including stilt and prop roots) that anchor them firmly and dissipate wave energy. This lets them withstand storm surges and tides without being uprooted, breaking the force of waves before they reach the shore.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question:
With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:
1. 'Commercial Paper' is a short-term unsecured promissory note.
2. 'Certificate of Deposit' is a long-term instrument issued by the Reserve Bank of India.
3. 'Call Money' is a short-term finance used for interbank transactions.
4. 'Zero-Coupon Bonds' are the interest-bearing short-term bonds issued by the Scheduled Commercial Banks to the corporations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1 is correct — commercial paper is a short-term unsecured promissory note. 3 is correct — call money is very short-term interbank borrowing. 2 is wrong — Certificates of Deposit are short-term instruments issued by banks/FIs, not long-term instruments issued by the RBI. 4 is wrong — zero-coupon bonds pay no periodic interest; they are issued at a discount.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question:
With reference to the Indian economy, demand-pull inflation can be caused/increased by which of the following?
1. Expansionary policies
2. Fiscal stimulus
3. Inflation-indexing wages
4. Higher purchasing power
5. Rising interest rates
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation arises when aggregate demand outpaces supply. Expansionary policies (1), fiscal stimulus (2) and higher purchasing power (4) all raise demand. Inflation-indexing wages (3) is a cost-push factor, and rising interest rates (5) reduce demand — so both dampen demand-pull inflation rather than cause it.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.question:
With reference to India's Desert National Park, which of the following statements are correct?
1. It is spread over two districts.
2. There is no human habitation inside the Park.
3. It is one of the natural habitats of the Great Indian Bustard.
questions.explanation: Desert National Park spreads across the Jaisalmer and Barmer districts of Rajasthan (statement 1 correct) and is a key habitat of the Great Indian Bustard (statement 3 correct). Statement 2 is wrong — several villages and human habitation exist inside the park.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.question: In the context of recent advances in human reproductive technology, 'Pronuclear Transfer' is used for
options: Fertilization of egg in vitro by the donor sperm
Development of stem cells into functional embryos
Prevention of mitochondrial diseases in offspring
questions.explanation: Pronuclear transfer is a mitochondrial replacement technique. The nuclear material from a fertilized egg with faulty mitochondria is transferred into a donor egg with healthy mitochondria, preventing the transmission of mitochondrial diseases to the child.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: The Global Competitiveness Report is published by the
options: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
questions.explanation: The Global Competitiveness Report, which ranks countries on the factors driving their productivity and prosperity, is published annually by the World Economic Forum (WEF).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is not a Harappan site?
questions.explanation: Chanhudaro, Kot Diji and Desalpur are all Indus Valley (Harappan) sites. Sohgaura in Uttar Pradesh is known for the Mauryan-era Sohgaura copper plate inscription, not for Harappan remains.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following relief sculpture inscriptions is 'Ranyo Ashoka' (King Ashoka) mentioned along with the stone portrait of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: At Kanganahalli (Karnataka), a relief sculpture depicts Ashoka with the inscription 'Ranyo Ashoka', one of the few places where the emperor is shown in a labelled portrait.

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Consider the following:
1. Deification of the Buddha
2. Treading the path of Bodhisattvas
3. Image worship and rituals
Which of the above is/are the feature/features of Mahayana Buddhism?
questions.explanation: All three are hallmarks of Mahayana Buddhism: the Buddha is deified and worshipped, the Bodhisattva ideal (seeking enlightenment for all beings) is central, and image worship and elaborate rituals are practised — unlike early Theravada tradition.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Building 'Kalyaana Mandapas' was a notable feature in the temple construction in the kingdom of
questions.explanation: Kalyana Mandapas (marriage halls, symbolising the divine marriage of the deity) were a distinctive addition to temple complexes under the Vijayanagara style of architecture.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to album and individual portrait?
questions.explanation: Jahangir, a great connoisseur of painting, moved the focus of the Mughal atelier away from illustrated manuscripts towards albums (muraqqa) and individual portraits, including detailed natural-history studies.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Atal Innovation Mission is set up under the
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), which promotes innovation and entrepreneurship through Atal Tinkering Labs and Atal Incubation Centres, is established under NITI Aayog.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: On 21st June, the Sun
options: does not set below the horizon at the Arctic Circle
does not set below the horizon at Antarctic Circle
shines vertically overhead at noon on the Equator
shines vertically overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn
questions.explanation: On 21st June (summer solstice), the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle experiences the midnight Sun — the Sun does not set below the horizon there. The Sun is overhead at the Equator only at the equinoxes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which one of the following groups of plants was domesticated in the 'New World' and introduced into the 'Old World'?
questions.explanation: Tobacco, cocoa and rubber are all native to the Americas (the New World) and were introduced to the Old World after Columbian contact. Coffee, sugarcane and wheat are Old World crops.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Asiatic lion is naturally found in India only.
2. Double-humped camel is naturally found in India only.
3. One-horned rhinoceros is naturally found in India only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct: the Asiatic lion survives in the wild only in India (Gir). The double-humped (Bactrian) camel occurs naturally across Central Asia, and the one-horned rhinoceros is also found in Nepal, so 'India only' is wrong for both.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Among the following, which one is the largest exporter of rice in the world in the last five years?
questions.explanation: India has been the world's largest exporter of rice in recent years, shipping both basmati and non-basmati varieties in volumes well ahead of Vietnam, Thailand and other competitors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why are dewdrops not formed on a cloudy night?
options: Clouds absorb the radiation released from the Earth's surface
Clouds reflect back the Earth's radiation
The Earth's surface would have low temperature on cloudy nights
Clouds deflect the blowing wind to ground level
questions.explanation: Dew forms when the ground cools enough (by radiating heat to the sky) to reach the dew point. On a cloudy night the clouds absorb the outgoing terrestrial (long-wave) radiation and re-radiate it back, so the surface does not cool sufficiently and dew does not form.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is issued by registered foreign portfolio investors to overseas investors who want to be part of the Indian stock market without registering themselves directly?
questions.explanation: Participatory Notes (P-Notes) are derivative instruments issued by registered Foreign Portfolio Investors to overseas investors who wish to invest in Indian markets without registering directly with SEBI.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Which of the following adopted a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
questions.explanation: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the European Union's data-protection and privacy law, adopted in April 2016 and enforced from 25 May 2018.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The word 'Denisovan' is sometimes mentioned in media in reference to
options: fossils of a kind of dinosaurs
a cave system found in North-East India
a geological period in the history of Indian subcontinent
questions.explanation: Denisovans are an extinct species/subspecies of archaic humans, first identified from fossil fragments found in the Denisova Cave in Siberia, known largely through ancient DNA analysis.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Recently, scientists observed the merger of giant 'blackholes' billions of light-years away from the Earth. What is the significance of this observation?
options: Possibility of inter-galactic space travel through 'wormhole' was confirmed
It enabled the scientists to understand 'singularity'
questions.explanation: The merger of massive black holes was significant because it produced gravitational waves — ripples in spacetime predicted by Einstein — which were directly detected (by LIGO), confirming his general theory of relativity.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: What is Cas9 protein that is often mentioned in news?
options: A molecular scissors used in targeted gene editing
A biosensor used in the accurate detection of pathogens in patients
A gene that makes plants pest-resistant
A herbicidal substance synthesized in genetically modified crops
questions.explanation: Cas9 is an enzyme that acts as 'molecular scissors' in the CRISPR-Cas9 system, cutting DNA at a guided location so that genes can be edited, removed or inserted.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: Hepatitis B virus is transmitted much like HIV
Hepatitis B, unlike Hepatitis C, does not have a vaccine
Globally, the number of people infected with Hepatitis B and C viruses are several times more than those infected with HIV
Some of those infected with Hepatitis B and C viruses do not show the symptoms for many years
questions.explanation: Statement (b) is incorrect and is therefore the answer: it is the other way round — Hepatitis B has an effective vaccine, whereas Hepatitis C has no vaccine. The other statements are correct.
